item.content:encoded:
I loved Rowsannah, and to me the AI subplot elevated this skip and made it a more interesting story. The protein mutation that makes people spontaneously explode (and is made worse by cellphone vibrations) is well written and could stand on its own. And there could have been some other way to sneak in the reveal that it was produced by non-anomalous genetic mutation, and likely will be so again. Would've been a +1 from me regardless on that front.

But Rowsannah was a great twist on the "AI murders humans due to not understanding human context" trope. Her actions were exactly correct, and Dr. Livi didn't give her time to explain before taking her autonomous functions offline. Livi simply assumed that Rowsannah had made an error. And the doctor's overreaction, while understandable, resulted in many more needless deaths. That's a kind of error which the Foundation can only guard against by individual vigilance. Creating or having control over something powerful, and being careless in deploying it because the human operator jumped to conclusions with inadequate data, is an irreducible danger to which the Foundation is uniquely vulnerable.

I really like the concept, and everything was well written…but I cannot stand Rowsannah. If I only consider everything before the Incident logs, it's an enthusiastic upvote. If I include the Incident logs, my instinct is to downvote.

I will go with option A and pretend the article ends after the Interview. +1
